sampling_model.design: Large-\(N\), fixed-\(T\) observational panel with a predeclared stopped-Hankel chart, polynomial frame, and cohort-time grid.
sampling_model.units: The panels \(W_i\) are independent draws from \(P_W\); within-panel dependence is generated by the untreated hidden Markov law and staggered adoption.
sampling_model.treatment: Adoption is absorbing and occurs with a current-hidden-state hazard before the period's untreated outcome, with fresh adoption randomization conditionally independent of future untreated innovations.
sampling_model.overlap: State hazards are interior and every target cohort has mass bounded away from zero on the inference stratum.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: All nuisance objects are finite stopped-word moments evaluated through one ordered Hankel minor fixed before outcomes and one fixed coefficient-normalized polynomial frame; no empirical latent labeling, rank-revealing minor selection, or adaptive frame search is used. The estimator is a total Borel map with sequential half-gap and uncovered-inverse gates and fixed fallback outputs. The Kim--Lee usability screen jointly bootstraps the same moment vector and applies only preregistered rank, gap, residual, cohort-mass, and ATT-half-width thresholds.

body.tldr: State-dependent adoption usually destroys parallel-trends comparisons because future untreated outcomes are missing precisely for selected latent states. A finite stopped-panel law nevertheless identifies every adopter cohort's untreated path law when the adoption hazard is constant within each current-emission alias class. Predictive rank yields a chart-independent minimal realization, while displayed coordinates and inference use one ordered Hankel minor fixed before outcomes and a total guarded estimator with a preregistered fallback. A generic legal fiber proves failure when aliased states have unequal hazards and forecasts; the exact positive \(T=5\), \(g=0\), \(r=1\) witness has ATT gap \(2/185\), and the local collision pair limits this proposal's plug-in at \(N^{-1/4}\). The exceptional \(K=3\) one-alias-block frontier and the Kim--Lee empirical certificate remain first-class open questions.

project_justification.gap: Staggered-DiD and interactive-fixed-effects methods use observed histories or adoption-date cohort moments. Causal latent-Markov procedures impose their own model-based latent recovery and ignorability structures, while HMM identification results either exclude exact aliasing or characterize latent ambiguity rather than observed-stopped-law-determined cohort continuation. Ordinary spectral results also do not select a preregistered stopped-Hankel minor.
project_justification.niche: The adoption event is an observable state-dependent mark. Its terminal vector can identify a similarity-invariant hazard operator even when positive non-permutation latent realizations fit the same stopped law; a fixed ordered minor is needed only to compute coordinates reproducibly, not to define the invariant.
project_justification.fill: The project proves hazard-lift path-law invariance, derives the generic converse and exact \(2/185\) stress test, supplies a total guarded fixed-chart estimator and regular-subset simultaneous inference, limits its own plug-in on an explicit collision path, and isolates both a concrete one-alias-block frontier and an operational empirical certificate as open questions.

body.related_work: Weiss and Nadler characterize non-permutation equivalence for HMMs with two aliased states; their similarities inform the legal fiber but do not target counterfactual cohort continuation. Allman, Matias, and Rhodes establish generic finite-window identification, while Gassiat, Cleynen, and Robin and Alexandrovich, Holzmann, and Leister use separation conditions that exclude exact repeated emissions. Bartolucci and Farcomeni provide a killed-forward latent event-history model without the proposed causal invariant. Pennoni, Paas, and Bartolucci use propensity-weighted hidden-Markov likelihood, and Clouth, Bijlsma, Pauws, and Vermunt use a fitted latent Markov measurement model inside a parametric g-formula. The generic converse diagnoses transporting those workflows to stopped panels while also demanding that continuation be determined by the observed stopped law: unequal within-alias hazards and forecasts preclude uniqueness absent another restriction. Those papers impose their own structural assumptions and are not contradicted, and the hazard-lift theorem does not identify their latent-state estimands. Callaway and Sant'Anna identify group-time ATT and simultaneous inference under conditional parallel trends. Callaway and Tsyawo use interactive fixed effects and adoption-date moments; their functional has neither a state-dependent stopping mark nor alias-fiber invariance, while hazard lifting does not impose their factor structure. Kim and Lee use observed-history matching in the six-period Netflix--IPTV panel, and Ishimaru uses repeated measurements outside evolving hidden selection. The exact pair is a stress test for transported fitted-state workflows and observed-history matching, not a contradiction of either paper because their assumptions are not asserted on the pair. Hsu, Kakade, and Zhang provide ordinary-HMM observable operators, but full predictive rank only ensures that some minor is nonsingular and does not validate the preregistered minor used here. Tran, Kim, and Doshi-Velez provide a moment-estimation template but not the stopped-chart, de-killing, or frame conditions. Andrews and Cheng provide weak-identification precedent; the collision proposition instead limits this proposal's fixed-chart plug-in and does not contradict the separated regular domains of Tran, Kim, and Doshi-Velez or Callaway and Sant'Anna. These sources are informed-by comparators, not results claimed to be strictly tightened.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The empirical algebra cannot be generated by exact commutativity or exact repeated eigenvalues after sampling noise perturbs population moments. The estimator therefore uses a fixed written-order polynomial dictionary and least-squares off-model extension. Full stopped-Hankel rank ensures that some \(K\)-minor works but not that the ordered \(H_{\mathcal U,\mathcal V}\) fixed before outcomes does; all Euclidean separation claims are tied to that declared chart and coefficient normalization. The total estimator uses inverse formulas only behind fixed half-gap gates and the uncovered-inverse threshold \(\tau_N=N^{-1/8}\), and otherwise returns fixed defaults. Along \(\eta_N=N^{-1/4}\) and \(\zeta_N=N^{-1}\), the omitted singular value is \((10.33271+o(1))\zeta_N\), the displayed product laws merge in total variation, and \(\tau_{0,1}\) remains separated at order \(N^{-1/4}\).
body.honest_scope: The point-identification theorem fixes the hidden order and a finite alphabet, uses \(T\ge2K-1\), assumes time-homogeneous untreated dynamics, invertible killed dynamics, positive cohort masses, and sequential hazard randomization. It identifies finite untreated cohort path laws but not latent labels, transitions, or initial probabilities. Predictive rank yields a chart-independent minimal realization and only guarantees existence of some nonsingular minor; the displayed formulas and inference additionally require the predeclared \(H_{\mathcal U,\mathcal V}\). The generic converse concerns future lags. The exact \(2/185\) witness and local lower bound apply only to \(K=3\), \(T=5\), \(g=0\), and \(r=1\). The lower bound limits this proposal's own fixed-chart plug-in and does not challenge comparator methods on their maintained regular domains. The total estimator has fixed fallback outputs, whose probability vanishes only on compact regular subsets. The open legal-lift classification is restricted to the positive interior binary \(K=3\), \(T=5\), one-two-state-alias-block stratum at \((g,r)=(0,1)\); it demands explicit branch invariants and a complexity improvement over generic elimination. The Kim--Lee data are unavailable, so no empirical certificate is claimed. Unknown order, continuous outcomes, approximate homogeneity, sharp tolerance bounds, adaptive chart selection, constrained-model efficiency, and finite-sample remainders remain open.
